A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same R1-zero-Div study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched reliably despite additions and relocation in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of 12 LLMs, mathematical benchmark results, diversity measurements, coefficient and model-size ablations, and training trajectories.

after.justification: v2 retains the original empirical study and adds sampled Avg@8 evaluations and GPQA Diamond results.

M1.justification: The token-level entropy objective, importance-weighted reformulation, restriction to positive samples, and combination with GRPO remain unchanged in Equations 7–12. No new model component or training procedure is introduced.

E1.justification: Appendix E.3 adds direct evaluation of the already trained models on GPQA Diamond, extending evaluation beyond the four original mathematical test sets. GSM8K training data and the original benchmark coverage remain unchanged.

E2.justification: The comparisons retain the base Qwen model, R1-zero, SimpleRL-Zoo, and Eurus-2-7B-PRIME. Removing Base- prefixes changes labels, not comparator identities. The added Avg@8 and GPQA comparisons use the same comparator set.

E3.justification: Section 5.2 adds an Avg@8 evaluation using eight responses per question at temperature 0.5, alongside the retained Pass@1 evaluation. Appendix E.3 also reports Avg@8 on GPQA. Existing training budgets, hyperparameters, and stated Pass@1 decoding settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: The coefficient-sensitivity evidence changes because the zero-diversity control average falls from 62.2 to 61.0: the unchanged lambda=0.05 result of 61.7 consequently moves from below to above the control (v1 Table 3; v2 Table 4). The tested coefficients, positive-versus-all comparison, model-size ablation, entropy curves, and solution case study are retained.

E5.justification: v1 provides accuracy point estimates without uncertainty estimates. v2 introduces explicitly identified standard errors for all five methods across the four main benchmarks in Table 2, substantially expanding uncertainty reporting. The eight responses per question are evaluation samples; neither PDF documents repeated training seeds or training-run uncertainty.

E6.justification: v2 adds a full Avg@8 comparison, with averages of 63.56 for R1-zero-Div and 60.06 for R1-zero, plus GPQA results of 34.3 and 32.7 respectively. Existing Pass@1 averages also change: R1-zero goes from 62.2 to 61.0 and Eurus-2-7B-PRIME from 63.2 to 62.1, while R1-zero-Div remains 64.4. These are substantial additions and revisions to reported evidence, not an improved same-setting score for the proposed method.

T1.justification: The definitions, gradient derivation, importance-sampling proof, and Potential@k discussion retain the same mathematics. Appendix A.1 rephrases the random-length argument as a rough idea but does not change its equations or reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution statements retain the diversity–Potential@k relationship, positive-sample diversity optimization, and claimed 3.5% improvement across four mathematical benchmarks. The revised baseline scores do not produce a corresponding revision of these central claims.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the new GPQA results as evidence of generalizability and adds a future extension to LLM tasks beyond reasoning in Section 7. Existing limitations concerning model scale and statistical versus user-intended diversity remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-code access link in the abstract and states in its checklist that code and instructions accompany the supplementary material. The disclosed software versions, hardware, training duration, system prompt, and hyperparameter table remain unchanged. The PDFs alone do not verify the linked resource.

R1.justification: v2 adds eight references covering evaluation reliability, policy diversity, and broader LLM applications. The evaluation references motivate Avg@8 reporting, while others support existing discussion or the new applicability outlook. The original references and central novelty positioning are retained.

P1.justification: The scientific narrative and section order remain largely unchanged. Local additions include the Avg@8 explanation, GPQA subsection, applicability sentence, acknowledgments, and NeurIPS checklist, together with updated affiliations and method labels. There is no extensive rewriting of the research argument.

P2.justification: v2 adds the Avg@8 and GPQA tables and moves the unchanged training-accuracy plot from main-text Figure 2 to appendix Figure 4. Other tables and figures are renumbered or repositioned, with shortened method labels and page reflow. The existing plots, system-prompt display, and solution example retain their content.

improvement.justification: The added Avg@8 comparison with standard errors and GPQA evaluation strengthen empirical support, while the project-code pointer improves reproducibility documentation. These gains are limited by unexplained revisions to baseline scores and an unchanged 3.5% Pass@1 improvement statement that no longer agrees with Table 1's averages of 64.4 versus 61.0. The method and theoretical support remain unchanged.
